_comment: Cascade spectacle (#187), read by screen code only. A heat tier is on once the cascade has lit minNodes dominoes or a cap of at least minCap (its value per trigger, from the capFired event) has gone off; the last tier on sets the colour and how many sparks trail each flow. While building, the same tiers read the board's node count and the biggest charge on an open end. Tier colours are 0xRRGGBB strings.

map._comment: The map screen (#306, M1). Everything on one paper sheet, floors left to right, the boss at the right end. Positions are screen pixels at 1920x1080. Stop discs: radius `stopR`, or `pickR` when the stop can be picked now; the 24 art pixel icon is drawn at `iconScale` times its size (whole numbers keep the pixels sharp). Roads are dots every `dotGap` pixels along a gentle curve; the road taken is a solid line. The paper is flat until the scroll (#307).

dominoLook.comment: Domino drawing (#217), read by src/game/dominoDrawing.ts. Positions are in mockup units (an amplifier bar is 100 high, the whole amplifier 216 wide, the socket on the left edge, the centre line at y 50); the screen size is units times unit. extent is each kind's width and height in units, for layout. Details (owner stripe, rarity gem, upgrade star) are hidden when the domino is shown below minDetailScale of full size; number, sockets and outputs always stay.

buildup.comment: Cascade build-up (#191). pitch.maxSteps: the pitch stops rising after this many cascade steps. glow: strength of the lit dominoes' glow, from litMin (first lit) to litMax (all lit). camera: boards with more than minNodes dominoes ease out (to zoomOut, or what fits the board mat, never below minZoom) and push in on a new biggest cap of at least push.minCap (push.reducedZoom with reduced flashing; no push with screen shake off); the camera never cuts off health, block or the intent card (keep: sizes of the boxes it protects and of an open end). The running counter and callouts it used to hold are now comboHype. Times are ms at 1x.

comfort.comment: Defaults for the menu comfort settings.

fx.comment: Code-drawn fallbacks for the effect textures (fx/<id>). glow and ring are always code-drawn.

projectiles.comment: The glow a domino takes in its owner's seat colour as the charge passes it, bigger and longer when a cap goes off (#189, read by seatGlow in src/game/projectiles.ts). The caps' effects now fly into the combo number (comboHype).

comboHype.comment: Cascade hype (#234, H1-H9), read by src/game/comboHype.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table, times in ms at 1x (all go through scaleTime). Arrays are indexed by tier 0..4. tiers: the combo total as a share of the enemy's line (B12); each threshold reached moves the number up one tier (highest wins when a hit crosses several), and reaching the line itself is the last tier (words[4], the combo:line cue). The number catches fire at the line; lethal is a bigger moment on top. smallHit: what an amplifier or junction hit does next to a cap's (spark size, arrival ring and punch as a share of a cap's). line: the meter under the number (scale: its full width is this many times the line; widthFraction of the board area; dy below the number's centre; holdMs: how long the table waits on a line reached by the last hit, before the slam). The number sits in the board area (combatLayout.board), centred across it and yFraction down it, and is shrunk to maxWidthFraction of the area's width. gap: the pause after each hit is start - step * hits so far, never below min (a depth step waits stepFraction of it). tierJump, lethal, slam and fanfare are the big moments; the slam's charge, flight, impact and fanfare together take about 2 s at the top tier. skip.factor scales the slam's times when a skipped cascade plays its short slam.

speedControl.comment: Combat playback speed button and its list (#220), read by src/game/speedControl.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table. Where the button sits comes from combatLayout.strip.speed (#302); the list opens upward, gap above it, and opens downward instead if it would leave the screen.

setOffPreview.comment: Set-off preview on the party's bar and shield (#222; the enemy's side was removed for 0.2, B8), read by src/game/setOffPreview.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table. The part of the party's health bar the set-off would take is the kit bar's pale part (no data). The bar and shield it draws on come from the bottom strip (combatLayout.strip, through the scene's refs). loss: the number over the bar's right end (dx from its right edge, dy from its top); gain: the block number over the shield; safe: the mark and word over the bar's left end (iconDx and textDx from the bar's left edge, dy from its top).

enemyReactions.comment: Enemy reactions (#190), read by src/game/enemyReactions.ts. Times are ms at 1x (scaled by playback speed), distances px on the 1920x1080 table. A hit of at least staggerMin damage staggers instead of flinching. The ghost bar waits delayMs after the last hit, then drains to the real value at perPointMs per point (between minMs and maxMs), so a run of hits shares one drain. Shield cracks show at each crack fraction of the block worn down.

fuseBoard.comment: Fuse board (#229), read by src/game/fuseBoard.ts. Lengths are px at the board scale (scale, a share of full size) and the whole tree shrinks together (never below minScale; 0.2 keeps the biggest tree, 12 dominoes, inside the arcane circle, #264) only when it outgrows its area. The owner stripe stays down to detailScale. gap: run between a domino's edge and the next one; rowPitch: distance between branches; ringRadius: the open-end ghost ring; padLeft: space left of the opener inside the area so its socket ring is not clipped; openerCharge: the charge an opener starts with (the engine's start charge, which no view exposes), only to colour a live number red or green on the opener slot; junctionGapX: where a junction's middle output (Hall of Mirrors) leaves, in domino units. fuse: dark under-stroke and spark-colour stroke widths, bend (share of the run used as the curve's handle), the cascade's burnt part (burnWidth, burnAlpha, burnMs at 1x). badge: the charge pill at a fuse's midpoint; nudge lists the places along the fuse (0..1) tried in order until it clears every tile, ring and other badge by clearance. ring: dashed open end, its gold charge badge, the legal highlight (pulse is skipped with reduced flashing); lock: the padlock on a locked end. live: the result bubble beside an end while a hand domino is hovered or dragged (good = at or above its base, bad = below it); dimAlpha for ends it is not aimed at. opener: the empty first slot.

handRow.comment: Your hand as a straight row (#253), read by src/game/handRow.ts; the seat-tab hands (combatLayout.tabs.hand) follow the same rule. No fan, tilt or overlap: dominoes sit gap px apart (between their real outlines), centred in area (the middle of the bottom strip, combatLayout.strip). scale: a hand domino's normal size; a hand too wide for the area shrinks evenly, never below minScale (about 80% of scale); past that it wraps into two rows, split by width as evenly as possible, rowGap px apart, at the size that fits both rows (the top row stays clear of the board: lower the board's bottom edge, combatLayout.board, if the area needs more height). The hovered domino grows to hoverScale and lifts by lift (tweenMs), drawn over its neighbours, which do not move; it never rises above the top of area, so a top-row domino lifts less (or grows downward) instead of covering the board. drag: the faint dashed place left by a dragged domino (the domino itself fades to holderAlpha). enter: a new draw slides in from the left edge of area (slideMs for an old domino finding its new place, enterMs for the new one, staggerMs between new ones).

combatLayout.comment: Combat screen layout (#302, one stage), read by CombatScene.ts, enemyUnit.ts, combatHud.ts, seatTabs.ts and handRow.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table; a box is x, y top-left with w, h; sizes that say grid are kit grid pixels (kit.unit screen pixels each). background: the converted table picture shown sharp at x3, and the soft dark edge over it. The arcane circle, the wizards on its left arc and the tree area are in battleWizards. enemy: the sprite stands with its feet at feet (moved left if its right edge would pass rightMargin), shown at scale screen pixels per art pixel, over a shadow (w is a share of the sprite width). block: the enemy block, top right (a kit plate: tier tag, name, passive and round chips that wrap, the health bar with the enemy block beside it, and the line as a number until the line bar comes). bubble: the action bubble over the head point (kept left of rightMargin, never above the block). action: one intent action in the bubble. strip: the bottom strip, a kit plate across the screen: party (health bar and block, round), speed and menu (where their buttons sit), pile (placements left, deck and used piles), hand (the hand row place), ready (the Ready button and how many are ready). tabs: the seat tabs, left of the enemy block until the racks replace them. board: the box the cascade camera frames and the combo number sits in. takeBack: the control on your own dominoes (size, offset from the domino top-left corner, how long it lingers, the room round the hand row where a dragged board domino counts as dropped on it). handFrame: the tab above the strip that names a hand that is not your own seat. note: a refusal by your hand (texts: what the host says, and what to show instead).

followUp.comment: The follow-up highlight (#295), read by handRow.ts, seatTabs.ts and CombatScene.ts: while a hand domino is hovered, picked or dragged, the dominoes (in the seat tabs and in your own hand) that could be placed on its open ends light up with a ring in glow (width px on screen: handWidth in your hand, tabWidth in the tabs; halo is the soft outer ring's alpha), and the rest fade to dimAlpha. Legality only (B8): no totals. Your own hand also lifts the hovered domino and dims unplayable ones; the ring is the extra mark there.

texts.illegal domino: That domino can't go there now
texts.can't take that node back: That one can't be taken back now
texts.a Ready player can't place or take back: You are Ready: press Ready again to change the board

wizardLook.comment: Choosing a wizard's look (#262), read by src/game/wardrobe.ts, the lobby lists and the single player start screen. Px on the 1920x1080 screen. wardrobe: the panel centred on the screen; everything inside is relative to its centre. preview: the big wizard (scale = screen px per art px, feet at x, y). swatches: the colour circles (size, pitch, row y, left x) and how many letters of a taker's name fit under one. tiles: the hat and robe choices, each on a small wizard (scale, tile size, pitch, left x, each row's centre y). lobbyList: rows of the online lobby (wizard scale, pitch, where the first row sits on the host and join screens, where the Edit button sits). startSeats: the single player seat cards (pitch between cards, top, size, wizard scale).

spells.comment: Spells, wards and the final spell in the cascade (#265), read by src/game/spells.ts, comboHype.ts and enemyReactions.ts. Sheets and frame timings are in data/wizard-art.json; here only the screen's own numbers. Times are ms at 1x (all go through scaleTime), distances px on the 1920x1080 table. flightMs: a damage spell's flight from its cap to the enemy card. impactOffsets: where each impact lands relative to the card's centre, [dx, dy], taken in turn by hit so spells in flight at once do not pile into one blob. flinchFactor: the enemy's small flinch at an impact, as a share of the hit flinch (enemyReactions.flinch). reducedAlpha: spells and impacts with reduced flashing. ward: a block cap's ward stands dy px in front of its owner's feet, rises from riseFrom px lower while it plays, the next ward of a cascade shifts by the next of offsets (x px), it fades over fadeMs when the cascade ends. final: the circle's final spell, scaled by the combo tier (scales) and tinted (tints, lethalTint on a kill, at lethalScale); reducedAlpha dims it with reduced flashing.

battleWizards.comment: The wizards and the arcane circle in battle (#264), read by src/game/arcaneCircle.ts, battleWizards.ts and seatTabs.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table. circle: where the circle sheet's centre stands (x, y; the sheet is drawn at the art scale, data/wizard-art.json), inner: the box the domino tree is fitted into (the fuse board's area; it keeps clear of the wizards on the rim), fadeMs: a tier fading into the next at 1x (through scaleTime), restMs: settling back to tier 0 after a cascade, beamFadeMs: the lethal beam fading in. reduced (reduced flashing): from tier minTier up the circle and the beam are drawn at alpha and their frames last at least minFrameMs, so nothing flickers. spots: the rim spots by party size, in seat order, each as a share of the circle's radius from its centre (x right, y down; the radius is wizard-art.json circle.radius). Every wizard faces right, towards the enemy (the top spot is a little lower than the mockup so its head clears the seat tabs). wizard: the shadow under the feet (w, h px, layers nested ellipses, alpha each), awayAlpha for an away seat, idleOffsetMs the idle loop's start by seat so they do not bob in step. marker: the YOU arrow over your own wizard (gap above the head, size, bob px and ms, outline). portrait: the seat tab's head and hat (crop is the idle frame's box in art px, scale screen px per art px, size the backing circle's radius).

text._comment: Text roles (#301, S6, T6). Each is a pixel font at a size on its pixel grid at 1920x1080 (screen pixels per font pixel: label 3, text 2, title 3, huge 6). A size no role has gets the nearest role (ties go to the smaller). The fonts are loaded from public/fonts/ before the first scene draws. Dominoes keep their own font (S7).

kit._comment: Interface kit (#301, T7), read by src/game/kit.ts. Sizes are in grid pixels: one grid pixel is `unit` screen pixels (3, the wizards' grid, T6). Colours are #rrggbb.
